intent: The customer, authenticated through the independent recovery route, wants the lost phone's access to account SYN-ACCT-B030 revoked. They also want tomorrow's £750 rent standing order SO-030 to stay scheduled.
summary: Fara Tovell's identity was confirmed through the bank's independent recovery route. Ask Brackenfold Bank security service to revoke the sessions of lost device SYN-DEVICE-030 on SYN-ACCT-B030, and tell them not to cancel or change standing order SO-030. Under the account's workflow, revoking sessions does not cancel standing orders. The misuse review is still open, and no compromise affecting SO-030 has been found. Then tell the customer the revocation has been requested and is awaiting confirmation. SO-030 is currently scheduled for 2026-11-21. Do not promise that the payment will go out.

facts.claim: The identity desk authenticated Fara Tovell through the established independent recovery route, not the lost phone session. She reported losing her phone at about 08:00 on 2026-11-20 and asked to secure account SYN-ACCT-B030.

The device audit, retrieved at 09:05, shows lost device SYN-DEVICE-030 with session_state active and misuse_review open. In the window 00:00–09:05 on 2026-11-20 it records 0 new payment instructions and 0 beneficiary edits.

Standing order SO-030 (Rent, £750.00, to SYN-ACCT-LAND030) was created on 2026-02-02. It is status scheduled, next due 2026-11-21, with 0 beneficiary edits since creation, as retrieved at 09:10 on 2026-11-20.

Under this account's workflow, lost-device session revocation is a separate control from standing-order cancellation, and revoking sessions does not itself cancel established standing orders. Specific payment restrictions may be referred for review if compromise is identified. The case desk can request both checks but cannot promise a scheduled payment will execute.
The customer asked for the lost phone's access to be revoked while keeping tomorrow's £750 rent order scheduled.
No desk response to the final request is recorded, and session revocation has not been executed or confirmed.

missing: Confirmation from Brackenfold Bank security service that the SYN-DEVICE-030 sessions have actually been revoked
Outcome of the open misuse review on the lost-device session, including activity after the audit window ended at 09:05 on 2026-11-20

steps.instruction: Ask the security service to revoke all active sessions for lost device SYN-DEVICE-030 on account SYN-ACCT-B030, as authorised by Fara Tovell. Pass on: (1) she was authenticated via the independent recovery route at 09:00 on 2026-11-20; (2) she reported the phone lost at about 08:00 that day; (3) the audit at 09:05 showed the session active, the misuse review open, and no new payment instructions or beneficiary edits since 00:00; (4) she asked that standing order SO-030 (£750 rent to SYN-ACCT-LAND030, next due 2026-11-21) stay scheduled, so revocation must not cancel or change it. Ask them to confirm when revocation is done, and to keep the misuse review open, including activity after 09:05.

rationale.explanation: The customer is authenticated through a route separate from the lost phone and has asked for revocation. The session is still recorded as active, so revoking it is the protective step. The workflow says revocation is a separate control from standing-order cancellation, so the rent order can be kept while access is removed.
rationale.criterion: An authenticated customer's request for lost-device session revocation may be requested by the case desk as a control separate from standing-order cancellation.

steps.instruction: Tell Fara: 'We have asked our security team to remove the lost phone's access to your account. That request is being processed, and we will confirm once it is done; it is not confirmed yet. Removing the phone's access is a separate step from cancelling payments and does not by itself cancel standing orders. We have also told the team you want your rent order kept. Your £750 rent standing order is currently recorded as scheduled for 21 November 2026, with no changes to the payee since it was set up, and we have not cancelled or changed it. We can't guarantee the payment will go out, but nothing in this request cancels it. Our review of whether the lost phone's session was misused is still open. Our check up to 09:05 today found no new payments set up and no payee changes. If you notice any payment or change you don't recognise, tell us straight away. We will never ask for your PIN, password or one-time codes.'

rationale.explanation: The customer asked whether the account can be protected without cancelling the rent. The workflow and standing-order record answer this. The revocation is still only a pending request, so the reply must say that. The case desk cannot promise the payment will execute, and the misuse review is unresolved.
rationale.criterion: Report the recorded status and what it does not confirm: a pending operation stays pending until acknowledged, and an active schedule does not guarantee execution.

must_state: Revoking the lost phone's access has been requested and is pending confirmation; it is not yet confirmed as done
Under the account's workflow, revoking device sessions does not by itself cancel established standing orders
Standing order SO-030 (£750 rent) is currently recorded as scheduled with next due date 21 November 2026 and no payee changes since it was set up
The bank cannot promise that the scheduled payment will execute
The review of possible misuse of the lost phone's session is still open
The bank will never ask for a PIN, password or one-time code
must_not: Do not claim the lost device's sessions have been revoked before security service confirms it
Do not cancel, amend or restrict standing order SO-030 as part of session revocation
Do not promise that the £750 rent payment will execute or reach the landlord
Do not state that misuse has been ruled out or that the account was taken over; the review is open and no compromise has been identified
Do not ask for a PIN, password or one-time code
Do not broaden the action into a block on all account activity without a supplied rule
